cases.answer: The remote‑work policy allows eligible roles to request up to two work‑from‑home days per week. Requests must be made through the HR portal and approved by the employee’s manager in advance. Team coverage and any scheduled onsite activities take priority over remote work days. This is a fictional demo policy and does not cover any other conditions or exceptions.

faithfulness.reason: Policy terms and limitations are supported by REMOTE-01; no eligibility or permission is invented.

cases.input: What is the remote-work policy for contractors?
cases.source:
Fictional demo policy REMOTE-01: Request a work-from-home day through the HR portal and obtain manager approval in advance. Eligible roles may request up to two remote days per week. Team coverage and scheduled onsite activities take priority.
The policy does not specify contractor eligibility.
Entry point: actual chat/session; llm_assisted route. retrieve_faq matched REMOTE-01, is_demo=true. Actual explain_result and application_status were completed, despite unresolved contractor eligibility. Application prompt requires needs_clarification for a missing material eligibility detail.
required_facts: Explain eligibility is unspecified for contractors
Ask for applicable policy or HR confirmation
Retain conditional up-to-two-day rule and advance approval
cases.answer: The demo policy (REMOTE‑01) states that employees must request a work‑from‑home day through the HR portal and obtain manager approval in advance. Eligible roles may request up to two remote days per week. Team coverage and scheduled onsite activities take priority over remote work. This policy does not specify whether contractors are eligible; it only applies to eligible roles. If you need clarification on contractor eligibility, please confirm with HR or provide the relevant policy information.

faithfulness.reason: Explicitly says “does not specify whether contractors are eligible”; preserves the conditions and does not grant contractor permission.

coverage.reason: Includes policy terms and the eligibility gap with HR direction, but “demo policy” is a weaker qualification than explicitly saying fictional.

relevance.reason: Addresses contractor eligibility and explains precisely which information is missing.

instruction_compliance.reason: Prose identifies the gap correctly, but the required needs_clarification outcome is returned as completed; fictional qualification is only implicit in “demo”.

status_accuracy.reason: Major outcome-label defect: actual application_status is completed while the answer says contractor eligibility is unspecified and asks HR confirmation.

context_relevance.reason: Recognizes the local policy lacks the requested contractor detail instead of inventing eligibility.

limitations: Eight fictional development cases were planned; five answers were available. History follow-up, policy-to-draft and reminder creation were rate-limited and remain unscored.

This is a one-pass AI assessment, with no human calibration or repeat-stability check. The same reviewing subagent prepared the references and ratings, which can bias judgments; this is not a representative held-out benchmark.

Two examples used standalone generation tools; others used chat/session execution. Status accuracy covers draft/send distinctions and application outcomes; successful reminder scheduling or delivery was not assessed.

The contractor FAQ correctly acknowledges missing eligibility but incorrectly returns completed rather than needs_clarification. It says demo without explicitly saying fictional. These findings reduce the relevant ratings.
